heroHeadline: Government sends 90-day state-of-exception extension to a divided Legislature and floats a state of siege as COB and Morales-aligned CSUTCB vow "permanent mobilization"
heroSubtitle: President Paz's cabinet formally approved Decree 5707 on Sept. 14, extending the state of exception in force since June 20 by 90 more days ahead of its Sept. 18-19 expiration; VP Edmand Lara convened the Legislative Assembly for a Sept. 16 vote, where COB executive secretary Mario Argollo called the extension "un atentado a la democracia" and the Morales-aligned CSUTCB declared "estado de emergencia y movilización permanente," setting a Sept. 26 national assembly to plan its response. Presidential spokesperson José Luis Gálvez said the same day the government could escalate further to a state of siege, including possible curfews, if new road blockades start. Separately, prosecutors expanded the case against detained presidential adviser Fernando Cerimedo on Sept. 9 to add usurpation-of-functions and money-laundering charges — his fourth concurrent case — as Nadia Beller alleged he "coordinated with law enforcement forces," while the floated boliviano eased for a fifth straight session to Bs. 10.99/$1 by Sept. 15 after Central Bank dollar sales.
